      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prop-committed-assembly",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a clearing stage with parameter $t$. Consider the finite sequence of its committed numerical states: the initial post-sweep state, indexed by $0$, and the states after successive successful clearings, indexed by $a=1,\\ldots,k_{\\max}$. Failed trials leave this numerical sequence unchanged. Let $A_a\\subset A_{a-1}$ be the active sites after operation $a$, put $O_a=A_{a-1}\\setminus A_a$, and let $T_a$ be the complement of $A_a$ in the physical torus.*\n\n*At each index use the physical state of Section <a href=\"#sec:state\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:state\">2</a>: the sites in $T_a$ have their exact true potentials, the sites in $A_a$ have their current partial potentials, and $M^{(a)}$ is the real terminal-Schur matrix. The relevant true terminal principal matrices are invertible at the fixed energy. Use the restriction of one frozen vector $r$ at every index, with $p=\\Im r$ bounded above and below by positive constants, and write $$g^{(a)}=(M^{(a)}-t\\mathop{\\mathrm{diag}}(r|_{A_a}))^{-1},\\qquad\n h^{(a)}=\\sqrt t\\,g^{(a)},\\qquad\n K^{(a)}_{ij}=(h^{(a)}_{ij})^2,\\qquad\n F^{(a)}_{ij}=|h^{(a)}_{ij}|^2.$$ Let $D_a$ be the Ward Laplacian of this state, so $$D_a(f)=\\frac12\\sum_{i,j\\in A_a}p_ip_jF^{(a)}_{ij}|f_i-f_j|^2.$$ With $q_i^{(a)}=\\Im g^{(a)}_{ii}$, the Ward identity gives $F^{(a)}p=q^{(a)}$. The word committed here identifies the numerical endpoints. The comparison at the initial endpoint is an input; its transport to later endpoints is the conclusion below.*\n\n\n*Assume at the initial state that, on potentials modulo constants, $$cW\\le D_0\\le CW,\\qquad\n \\max_{i\\in A_0}\\sum_{j\\in A_0}|h^{(0)}_{ij}|^4\n \\le .7H_*,\\qquad\n \\max_{i\\in A_0}|g^{(0)}_{ii}-r_i|\\le Ct^{.42\\delta}.\n \\label{eq:assembly-initial-data}$$ Here $H_*=t^{1+\\delta}$ and $W(f)=\\inf_{f=\\alpha+v|_{A_0}}\n (\\|\\alpha\\|_2^2+b^{-1}\\|\\nabla v\\|_2^2)$, with $b=t_{n_0}t$.*\n\n*Assume also the geometric bounds supplied by Lemma <a href=\"#lem:clearing-locality\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:clearing-locality\">34</a>. For $D_s\\asymp t^{-8-\\nu}$, each $O_a$ lies in the ball of radius $D_s$ about its anchor $z_a$ and has size at most $Cn_h$, where $n_h=\\lfloor t^{-1-.46\\delta}\\rfloor$. The anchors are distinct. The cube halos $Q_a,Q'_a$ of radii $100D_s,200D_s$ are embedded lattice cubes in the torus, and each family has overlap at most $Ct^{-d\\nu}$. At every indexed state, $|A_a|\\ge N/2$ and $$d_{T_a}(u,v)\\ge\\tfrac12\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}(u,v)-m',\\qquad m'\\le t^{-1.03}.$$*\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n*For each operation set $$a^{(a)}=h^{(a)}-h^{(a-1)}|_{A_a\\times A_a}.$$ Assume these actual survivor differences satisfy $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\max_{i,j\\in A_a}|a^{(a)}_{ij}|\n &\\le C\\sqrt t\\,t^{.42\\delta},\\notag\\\\\n \\max_{i\\in A_a}\\sum_{j\\in A_a}|a^{(a)}_{ij}|^2\n &\\le Ct^{.25\\delta},\\qquad\n \\sum_{i,j\\in A_a}|a^{(a)}_{ij}|^2\n \\le Ct^{-1-.47\\delta}.\n \\label{eq:assembly-single-distortions}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Assume further that, with constants $c,C>0$ and a fixed $P$, $$|a^{(a)}_{ij}|\n \\le t^{-P}\\exp\\!\\left\\{-ct\\left[\n (\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}(i,O_a)-Cm')_++(\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}(j,O_a)-Cm')_+\n \\right]\\right\\}.\n \\label{eq:assembly-single-decay}$$ Then, for all sufficiently small $t$, every prefix $0\\le k\\le k_{\\max}$ satisfies $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\|K^{(k)}\\|&\\le\\|K^{(0)}\\|+t^{.10\\delta},\n \\label{eq:assembly-K-output}\\\\\n \\max_{i\\in A_k}|g^{(k)}_{ii}-r_i|\n &\\le Ct^{.42\\delta-d\\nu}=o(t^{.36\\delta}),\n \\label{eq:assembly-lag-output}\\\\\n \\max_{i\\in A_k}\\left(\\sum_{j\\in A_k}|h^{(k)}_{ij}|^4\\right)^{1/4}\n &\\le\\left(.7^{1/4}+Ct^{.0225\\delta-d\\nu}\\right)H_*^{1/4}\n <(.8H_*)^{1/4}.\n \\label{eq:assembly-row-output}\n\\end{aligned}$$ All Schur complements in the successive definition $$L_a=D_a-\\mathop{\\mathrm{Schur}}_{O_a}D_{a-1}\\quad\\hbox{on }A_a$$ exist, and each $D_a$ has precisely the constant kernel. Extend each $L_a$ by zero to $A_0$. Then $$\\left|\\sum_{a=1}^k L_a\\right|\n \\le t^{.10\\delta}D_0\n \\label{eq:assembly-energy-output}$$ in quadratic forms. In particular, writing $X_k=D_k^+$, every neutral charge $y$ supported in $A_k$ satisfies $$(1+t^{.10\\delta})^{-1}X_0(y)\n \\le X_k(y)\\le\n (1-t^{.10\\delta})^{-1}X_0(y),\n \\label{eq:assembly-inverse-output}$$ where $y$ is extended by zero in $X_0(y)$. All constants are uniform in the number of components and the torus volume.",
        "source_id": "PM-261.1"
      },

        {
          "anchor": "stmt-prop-committed-assembly",
          "exact_quote": "Fix a clearing stage with parameter $t$. Failed trials leave this numerical sequence unchanged. Let $A_a\\subset A_{a-1}$ be the active sites after operation $a$, put $O_a=A_{a-1}\\setminus A_a$, and let $T_a$ be the complement of $A_a$ in the physical torus.*\n\n*At each index use the physical state of Section <a href=\"#sec:state\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:state\">2</a>: the sites in $T_a$ have their exact true potentials, the sites in $A_a$ have their current partial potentials, and $M^{(a)}$ is the real terminal-Schur matrix. The relevant true terminal principal matrices are invertible at the fixed energy. Use the restriction of one frozen vector $r$ at every index, with $p=\\Im r$ bounded above and below by positive constants, and write $$g^{(a)}=(M^{(a)}-t\\mathop{\\mathrm{diag}}(r|_{A_a}))^{-1},\\qquad\n h^{(a)}=\\sqrt t\\,g^{(a)},\\qquad\n K^{(a)}_{ij}=(h^{(a)}_{ij})^2,\\qquad\n F^{(a)}_{ij}=|h^{(a)}_{ij}|^2.$$ Let $D_a$ be the Ward Laplacian of this state, so $$D_a(f)=\\frac12\\sum_{i,j\\in A_a}p_ip_jF^{(a)}_{ij}|f_i-f_j|^2.$$ With $q_i^{(a)}=\\Im g^{(a)}_{ii}$, the Ward identity gives $F^{(a)}p=q^{(a)}$. The word committed here identifies the numerical endpoints. The comparison at the initial endpoint is an input; its transport to later endpoints is the conclusion below.*\n\n\n*Assume at the initial state that, on potentials modulo constants, $$cW\\le D_0\\le CW,\\qquad\n \\max_{i\\in A_0}\\sum_{j\\in A_0}|h^{(0)}_{ij}|^4\n \\le .7H_*,\\qquad\n \\max_{i\\in A_0}|g^{(0)}_{ii}-r_i|\\le Ct^{.42\\delta}.\n \\label{eq:assembly-initial-data}$$ Here $H_*=t^{1+\\delta}$ and $W(f)=\\inf_{f=\\alpha+v|_{A_0}}\n (\\|\\alpha\\|_2^2+b^{-1}\\|\\nabla v\\|_2^2)$, with $b=t_{n_0}t$.*\n\n*Assume also the geometric bounds supplied by Lemma <a href=\"#lem:clearing-locality\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:clearing-locality\">34</a>. For $D_s\\asymp t^{-8-\\nu}$, each $O_a$ lies in the ball of radius $D_s$ about its anchor $z_a$ and has size at most $Cn_h$, where $n_h=\\lfloor t^{-1-.46\\delta}\\rfloor$. The anchors are distinct. The cube halos $Q_a,Q'_a$ of radii $100D_s,200D_s$ are embedded lattice cubes in the torus, and each family has overlap at most $Ct^{-d\\nu}$. At every indexed state, $|A_a|\\ge N/2$ and $$d_{T_a}(u,v)\\ge\\tfrac12\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}(u,v)-m',\\qquad m'\\le t^{-1.03}.$$*\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n*For each operation set $$a^{(a)}=h^{(a)}-h^{(a-1)}|_{A_a\\times A_a}.$$ Assume these actual survivor differences satisfy $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\max_{i,j\\in A_a}|a^{(a)}_{ij}|\n &\\le C\\sqrt t\\,t^{.42\\delta},\\notag\\\\\n \\max_{i\\in A_a}\\sum_{j\\in A_a}|a^{(a)}_{ij}|^2\n &\\le Ct^{.25\\delta},\\qquad\n \\sum_{i,j\\in A_a}|a^{(a)}_{ij}|^2\n \\le Ct^{-1-.47\\delta}.\n \\label{eq:assembly-single-distortions}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Assume further that, with constants $c,C>0$ and a fixed $P$, $$|a^{(a)}_{ij}|\n \\le t^{-P}\\exp\\!\\left\\{-ct\\left[\n (\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}(i,O_a)-Cm')_++(\\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}(j,O_a)-Cm')_+\n \\right]\\right\\}.\n \\label{eq:assembly-single-decay}$$ Then, for all sufficiently small $t$, every prefix $0\\le k\\le k_{\\max}$ satisfies $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\|K^{(k)}\\|&\\le\\|K^{(0)}\\|+t^{.10\\delta},\n \\label{eq:assembly-K-output}\\\\\n \\max_{i\\in A_k}|g^{(k)}_{ii}-r_i|\n &\\le Ct^{.42\\delta-d\\nu}=o(t^{.36\\delta}),\n \\label{eq:assembly-lag-output}\\\\\n \\max_{i\\in A_k}\\left(\\sum_{j\\in A_k}|h^{(k)}_{ij}|^4\\right)^{1/4}\n &\\le\\left(.7^{1/4}+Ct^{.0225\\delta-d\\nu}\\right)H_*^{1/4}\n <(.8H_*)^{1/4}.\n \\label{eq:assembly-row-output}\n\\end{aligned}$$ All Schur complements in the successive definition $$L_a=D_a-\\mathop{\\mathrm{Schur}}_{O_a}D_{a-1}\\quad\\hbox{on }A_a$$ exist, and each $D_a$ has precisely the constant kernel. Extend each $L_a$ by zero to $A_0$. Then $$\\left|\\sum_{a=1}^k L_a\\right|\n \\le t^{.10\\delta}D_0\n \\label{eq:assembly-energy-output}$$ in quadratic forms. In particular, writing $X_k=D_k^+$, every neutral charge $y$ supported in $A_k$ satisfies $$(1+t^{.10\\delta})^{-1}X_0(y)\n \\le X_k(y)\\le\n (1-t^{.10\\delta})^{-1}X_0(y),\n \\label{eq:assembly-inverse-output}$$ where $y$ is extended by zero in $X_0(y)$.         "exact_quote": "Let $g=(M-t\\mathop{\\mathrm{diag}}r)^{-1}$ on a nonempty active set, where $M$ is real symmetric, $r$ is bounded, and $0<c\\le p_i=\\Im r_i\\le C$. Suppose $q_i=\\Im g_{ii}\\le C$, the lag $e'=\\mathop{\\mathrm{diag}}(g)-r$ satisfies $\\|e'\\|_\\infty=o(t^{.36\\delta})$ uniformly in the construction parameters, and $$\\|K\\|<\\tfrac12,\\qquad\n \\|(I-K)^{-1}\\|_{\\infty\\to\\infty}\\le C\\log(1/t).$$ For small $t$ there is a measurable vector $\\zeta$, with $\\|\\zeta\\|_\\infty\\le t^{.35\\delta}$, such that for $r'=r+\\zeta$ and $g'=(M-t\\mathop{\\mathrm{diag}}r')^{-1}$ one has $g'_{ii}=r'_i$. Writing $\\rho=\\|\\zeta\\|_\\infty$, the changes satisfy $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\max_i\\|\\Delta h_i\\|_2&\\le C\\rho,\n &\\max_{i,j}|\\Delta h_{ij}|&\\le C\\sqrt t\\,\\rho,\n &\\max_i\\|\\Delta h_i\\|_4&\\le Ct^{1/4}\\rho,\n \\label{eq:assembly-reset-rows}\\\\\n \\|K'-K\\|&\\le C\\rho,\n &(1-C\\rho)D&\\le D'\\le(1+C\\rho)D.\n \\label{eq:assembly-reset-forms}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Here $D'$ uses $p'=\\Im r'$, which remains in a fixed positive bounded range.         "exact_quote": "Choose the fixed energy window and the initialization constants as in Proposition <a href=\"#prop:initialization\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:initialization\">10</a>. For sufficiently large $n_0$, uniformly in $m\\ge4n_0$ and in the fixed energy in that window, the following statements hold along every finite history produced by the ordinary-sweep and clearing rules, with failed trials rolled back. At each completed stage start the diagonal fixed-point relation, the three comparisons <a href=\"#eq:comparators\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:comparators\">[eq:comparators]</a>, the fourth-row bound $\\max_i\\sum_j|h_{ij}|^4\\le t^{1+\\delta}$, and $\\|K\\|\\le1/3$ hold. The vectors $r$ remain bounded with their imaginary parts in one fixed positive bounded range. The low comparison constants remain in fixed positive bounded ranges, and the rough high constant $C_0$ can be chosen independently of the stage. The kernel of $D$ consists of the constants, at least $N/2$ sites remain active, and the terminal metric satisfies <a href=\"#eq:assembly-terminal-metric\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:assembly-terminal-metric\">[eq:assembly-terminal-metric]</a>.*\n\n*During a clearing stage, every committed prestate has lag $o(t^{.36\\delta})$, fourth-row sums below $.8t^{1+\\delta}$, and the comparison bounds furnished by Proposition <a href=\"#prop:committed-assembly\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:committed-assembly\">35</a>. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Anderson lattice Hamiltonian** ([source](#eq:model)): For $\lambda>0$, define the bounded self-adjoint operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^d)$ by $$\label{eq:model} (H_{\lambda,\omega}\psi)(x) =-\sum_{j=1}^d\bigl(\psi(x+\mathbf e_j)+\psi(x-\mathbf e_j)\bigr) +\lambda V_x(\omega)\psi(x).$$
- **Active sites** ([source](#pm-h-10)): Active sites retain artificial damping.
- **Committed terminal sites** ([source](#pm-h-10)): A committed terminal site has its exact true potential, has been Schur-eliminated, and never changes again.
- **Pending active sites** ([source](#pm-h-10)): A pending site’s partial value may contain auxiliary digits, and the construction makes no freshness claim for its true suffix.
- **Retained operation filtration** ([source](#pm-h-11)): Number the successive queries and completed measurable decisions by $q=1,2,\ldots$, and let $\mathcal F_q^{\mathrm{ret}}$ be the information retained after operation $q$.
- **Schur complement convention** ([source](#pm-h-12)): Throughout, the subscript in a Schur complement names the *eliminated* indices: if $R$ is the complement of $\mathcal E$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Schur}}_{\mathcal E} B =B_{RR}-B_{R\mathcal E}B_{\mathcal E\mathcal E}^{-1}B_{\mathcal ER}.$$
- **Neutral charges** ([source](#pm-h-12)): Its pseudoinverse $X=D^+$ is then an inverse on neutral charges, namely vectors $y$ with $\sum_i y_i=0$.
- **Dual spatial comparison forms** ([source](#stmt-lem-dual-forms)): For $b>0$, define $$\begin{split} W(f)&=\inf_{f=\alpha+\mathcal Cv} \bigl(\\|\alpha\\|_2^2+b^{-1}\\|\nabla v\\|_2^2\bigr),\\ W^*(y)&=\\|y\\|_2^2+ b\langle y_\Sigma,\Lambda^+y_\Sigma\rangle, \qquad \sum_{x\in\mathcal A}y_x=0. \end{split}$$
- **Transformed diagonal lag** ([source](#pm-h-26)): We call $g_{\rm diag}-r$ the raw diagonal error and $\widetilde U=P(g_{\rm diag}-r)$ its transformed lag.
- **Collapsed terminal pseudometric** ([source](#pm-h-42)): Assign cost zero to each nearest-neighbor edge meeting a terminal site, and cost one to every other nearest-neighbor edge.
- **Ridge leverage scores** ([source](#subsec:clearing-algebra)): For a ridge parameter $\tau>0$, define $$\label{eq:clearing-ridge} G_\tau=\Gamma+\tau I,\qquad U=\mathcal C G_\tau^{-1/2},\qquad m_i=\\|u_i\\|^2\quad(i\in R),$$ where $u_i$ is the $i$-th row of $U$.
- **Birth labels** ([source](#pm-h-75)): A *birth* is a first tile-trial failure in a one-digit sweep or a failed clearing trial.
- **Finite-box disorder threshold** ([source](#stmt-def-threshold)): For the fixed dimension $d\ge4$, let $n_*(d)$ be the least integer $k\ge10$ with the following property. For every pair of integers $n_0\ge k$ and $m\ge4n_0$, every $u\in(1/4,1]$, and every $E\in I_d=-2d+(1/200,1/100)$, set $$L=4^{20m},\qquad N=L^d,\qquad \lambda(n_0,u)=\sqrt{3u}\,2^{-n_0},\qquad \eta=u4^{-m}.$$ Let $H_{m,n_0,u}$ be the true periodic negative-hopping Anderson matrix on $(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d$ with independent uniform $[-1,1]$ variables and coupling $\lambda(n_0,u)$. With probability at least $1/2$, there must exist a set $A$ and coefficients $r=(r_i)_{i\in A}$ such that $$\begin{gathered} \|A\|\ge N/2,\qquad \|r_i\|\le k,\qquad \Im r_i\ge1/k\quad(i\in A),\\ G_A^{\rm cert}:= (H_{m,n_0,u}-E-\eta\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}_A r)^{-1}\ \text{exists},\qquad \Im(G_A^{\rm cert})_{ii}\ge1/k\quad(i\in A). \end{gathered} \label{eq:threshold-criterion}$$ The probability here is taken only over the true site variables. Define $$\lambda_d=\sqrt3\,2^{-n_*(d)}. \label{eq:threshold-lambda}$$

        {
          "anchor": "eq:spectral-cut-rank",
          "exact_quote": "For $0<\\epsilon\\le1$, define $$Q=\\chi_{[E-\\epsilon\\eta,E+\\epsilon\\eta]}(H_m),\\quad\n r_Q=\\operatorname{rank}Q,\\quad\n T_c=T(I-Q),\\quad B_c=P_AT_cP_A,\\quad G_c=f_\\eta(B_c).$$ The identity $$B_A-B_c=P_ATQ P_A$$ shows that $\\operatorname{rank}(B_A-B_c)\\le r_Q$, for every set $A$. For self-adjoint matrices $B,C$, $$f_\\eta(B)-f_\\eta(C)\n =(I-i\\eta B)^{-1}(B-C)(I-i\\eta C)^{-1}.$$ Thus $D=G_A-G_c$ has $$\\label{eq:spectral-cut-rank}\n \\operatorname{rank}D\\le r_Q,\\qquad\n \\|D\\|\\le2/\\eta,\\qquad\n \\|D\\|_{\\mathrm{HS}}^2\\le4r_Q/\\eta^2.$$ Put $M_\\epsilon=1+\\epsilon^{-2}$. Since $Q$ commutes with $T$, the matrix $T_c$ is self-adjoint, and so is its compression $B_c$ on $\\ell^2(A)$. Its own functional calculus gives $$G_c^*G_c=B_c^2(I+\\eta^2B_c^2)^{-1}\\le B_c^2.$$ Together with contraction of the coordinate projection this implies $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\eta\\|G_ce_i\\|^2\n &\\le\\eta\\|B_ce_i\\|^2\\le\\eta\\|T_ce_i\\|^2\\notag\\\\\n &\\le M_\\epsilon q_i^{(m)}(E+i\\eta),\\qquad i\\in A.\n \\label{eq:spectral-cut-column}\n\\end{aligned}$$ For the last inequality, outside the cut interval one has $\\eta/(u-E)^2\\le M_\\epsilon\\eta/((u-E)^2+\\eta^2)$. The argument neither commutes $P_A$ past $Q$ nor uses an operator-monotonicity assertion about $f_\\eta$.",

## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-retained-freshness** [claim](#stmt-lem-conditional-freshness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-conditional-freshness): Factor the independent coordinate laws after each predictable query, then pass to stopped histories. -> Conditional laws for unqueried inputs at reached stopping times.
- **step-dual-forms** [claim](#stmt-lem-dual-forms) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-dual-forms): Complete squares on the quotient by constants. -> Dual forms and inverted comparison inequalities.
- **step-fourier-charge** [claim](#stmt-lem-fourier-charge) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-fourier-charge): Split Fourier frequencies and balance the resulting norm bounds. -> Uniform mixed-norm inverse-energy bound.
- **step-weighted-cubes** [claim](#stmt-lem-cube-weight) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cube-weight): Reflect a cube to a torus and split its centered Fourier modes. -> Weighted and unweighted cube inequalities.
- **step-lattice-counting** [claim](#stmt-lem-lattice-counting) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-lattice-counting): Count minimal displacement representatives and sum distance shells. -> Ball-volume and exponential-moment estimates independent of torus size.
- **step-free-density** [claim](#stmt-lem-initial-bottom-density) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-initial-bottom-density): Use bottom-coordinate polar integration, localized density subtraction, and integration by parts. -> Positive boundary density and logarithmic resolvent integral bounds.
- **step-initialization** [claim](#stmt-prop-initialization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-initialization): Construct a contracting scalar fixed point and prove discrete Fourier gap comparisons directly at small grid frequencies. -> Initial self-consistent state with slack in all invariant bounds.
- **step-port-duplication** [claim](#stmt-lem-duplication) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-duplication): Factor the virtual matrices through physical site maps and dualize the exact duplicated energy. -> Port Ward identity and exact reserve target forms.
- **step-single-deletion** [claim](#stmt-lem-single-update) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-single-update): Apply the rank-one inverse identity and compare squared entries with scalar Schur pivots. -> Exact correction increments and scalar moment expansions.
- **step-prestate-bounds** [claim](#stmt-lem-sweep-prestate) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sweep-prestate): Combine Ward mass, transformed lag, weighted operator estimates, and the sharp inverse-form bound. -> Analytic estimates for every remaining port set.
- **step-correction-stacks** [claim](#stmt-lem-sweep-j) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sweep-j): Sum signed means and bound both operator square stacks. -> Subset-uniform correction mean, variance, and jump controls.
- **step-laplacian-stacks** [claim](#stmt-lem-sweep-laplacian) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sweep-laplacian): Use weighted commutator cancellation, output stacks, and charge interpolation. -> Relative mean and dual square-stack controls.
- **step-transformed-lag** [claim](#stmt-lem-sweep-lag) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sweep-lag): Derive the exact survivor lag equation and bound its masked inverse and nonlinear series. -> Lag square stack and signed summed conditional mean.
- **step-row-proxies** [claim](#stmt-lem-sweep-fourth) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sweep-fourth): Expand fourth powers and use the cubic Ward-row gain. -> Proxy mean and square bounds for full and reserve rows.
- **step-increment-package** [claim](#stmt-prop-sweep-increments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-sweep-increments): Pull energy increments to a fixed Hilbert space and average candidate slots only after establishing subset bounds. -> Stopped concentration input package.
- **step-collapsed-decay** [claim](#stmt-lem-locality) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-locality): Conjugate by exponential weights constant across terminal shortcuts. -> Collapsed and ordinary spatial resolvent decay.
- **step-inverse-row** [claim](#stmt-lem-inverse-row) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-inverse-row): Use weighted contraction for long powers and Ward row mass for short powers. -> Absolute inverse-row and entrywise inverse decay bounds.
- **step-prospective-update** [claim](#stmt-lem-local-prospective) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-local-prospective): Retain damping and use jump bounds to establish a poststate margin before testing fine caps. -> Well-defined candidate output and localized increments through a first breaking step.
- **step-local-pullback** [claim](#stmt-lem-local-pullback) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-local-pullback): Use cutoffs, cube Poincare control, and duality in a fixed local inner product. -> Local operator mean and identity square bounds.
- **step-budget-transfer** [claim](#stmt-lem-local-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-local-transfer): Sum near records by bounded overlap and bound discarded kernels by exponential tails. -> Strict global mutable caps and reserve-row output.
- **step-matrix-concentration** [claim](#stmt-lem-matrix-concentration) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-matrix-concentration): Construct a trace-exponential supermartingale using predictable scalar envelopes and stop at eigenvalue crossings. -> Maximal concentration inequality.
- **step-local-trial** [claim](#stmt-lem-local-trial) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-local-trial): Include the first breaking update in the stopped stream, verify identity variance bounds, and union over fixed local tests. -> Uniform conditional trial failure estimate.
- **step-sweep-endpoint** [claim](#stmt-prop-ordinary-sweep) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-ordinary-sweep): Use successive conditioning for retries and express accepted endpoint forms in reserve physical normalization. -> Reduced-scale endpoint bounds and conditional first-trial failure control.
- **step-core-completion** [claim](#stmt-lem-core-completion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-core-completion): Factor the survivor change through the scattering cross-block range and apply unitarity. -> Deterministic survivor distortion bounds for arbitrary obtained true core values.
- **step-range-localization** [claim](#stmt-lem-clearing-range-localization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-clearing-range-localization): Apply exponential conjugation to the exterior equation and bound each range vector by its own norm. -> Localization of the full range without singular-value lower bounds.
- **step-core-decay** [claim](#stmt-cor-core-decay) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-core-decay): Apply range projection decay at both endpoints of the supported scattering change. -> Spatial decay of the completed core's survivor change.
- **step-leverage-drift** [claim](#stmt-lem-leverage-drift) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-leverage-drift): Use unitary cancellation, a small Gram increment, and exact congruence normalization. -> Negative conditional squared-leverage drift.
- **step-heat-count** [claim](#stmt-lem-clearing-heat-count) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-clearing-heat-count): Combine nonpositive ridge motion with heat drift, then iterate conditional count bounds over blocks. -> Expected remaining heat count and exponential tail.
- **step-clearing-preparation** [claim](#stmt-prop-clearing-trial) / [proof](#pm-h-58): Track distortion and varying-ridge leverage streams through the breaking step, localize monitoring, and combine count and martingale tails. -> Measurable preparation with controlled failure and full projection target on success.
- **step-separated-metric** [claim](#stmt-lem-assembly-metric) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-assembly-metric): Compare old and new costs along a simple path and count transitions between separated groups. -> Metric lower bound after adding all groups.
- **step-clearing-locality** [claim](#stmt-lem-clearing-locality) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-clearing-locality): Induct over proposed pivots using full-range localization and sum separated-group geometric losses. -> Metric, pivot-location, active-count, and halo-overlap bounds.
- **step-committed-assembly** [claim](#stmt-prop-committed-assembly) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-committed-assembly): Telescope committed differences and separately bound survivor-edge changes and old energy through deleted coordinates. -> Uniform committed lag, row, correction, and inverse-form comparisons.
- **step-diagonal-reset** [claim](#stmt-prop-reset) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-reset): Solve the reset equation by contraction and control energy by weighted commutator identities. -> Measurable self-consistent diagonal with controlled analytic costs.
- **step-stage-induction** [claim](#stmt-prop-deterministic-induction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-deterministic-induction): Use summable scale errors and reserve coefficient slack to close all enlarged invariant ranges. -> Uniform pathwise stage bounds for every finite reached history.
- **step-pending-witnesses** [claim](#stmt-prop-witness-bound) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-witness-bound): Extract separated deterministic witness trees with distinct leaf labels and close the weighted entropy recursion. -> Small pending probability at every site before the cutoff.
- **step-certificate-completion** [claim](#stmt-prop-certificate) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-witness-bound-2): Remove pending sites with high probability, bound late first-trial failures, and insert every untouched true suffix in the final sweep. -> Finite-volume certificate entirely in the true potential variables.
- **step-intrinsic-threshold** [claim](#stmt-prop-threshold) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-threshold): Project compact determinant-bounded feasibility sets and invoke uniform construction bounds. -> Borel feasibility and a positive intrinsic disorder threshold.
- **step-own-site-averaging** [claim](#stmt-lem-spectral-averaging) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-spectral-averaging): Integrate the scalar cavity Poisson kernel and pass to spectral measures by regularity. -> Conditional spectral averaging bound.
- **step-spectral-readout** [claim](#stmt-prop-certificate-readout) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-certificate-readout): Cut the true spectral projection, control its expected rank by unconditional own-site averaging, pass to infinite volume, propagate boundary positivity, and remove exceptional singular mass. -> Pure absolute continuity, spectrum inclusion, and positive root spectral weight.
- **step-main-spectral-result** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-certificate-readout-2): Apply the spectral readout to the constructed certificate and the dimension-appropriate threshold. -> The claimed fixed-coupling absolutely continuous spectral interval.
- **step-edge-coexistence** [claim](#stmt-cor-coexistence) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-coexistence): Intersect the fixed-coupling delocalization event with the cited edge-localization and spectrum events. -> Disjoint nontrivial absolutely continuous and localized spectral intervals at the same coupling.

          "anchor": "stmt-lem-sweep-lag",
          "exact_quote": "Let $t>0$ be sufficiently small, $\\beta=.42\\delta$, and $H_*=t^{1+\\delta}$. At a fixed prestate, suppose that $h=h^\\top$, $g=h/\\sqrt t$, $K_{ij}=h_{ij}^2$, $F_{ij}=|h_{ij}|^2$, and $$\\label{eq:sweep-lag-prestate}\n\\begin{gathered}\n \\max_i\\sum_jF_{ij}\\le C,\\qquad\n \\max_i\\sum_jF_{ij}^2\\le H_*,\\qquad\n \\|h\\|\\le Ct^{-1/2},\\qquad\n \\max_i|h_{ii}|\\le C\\sqrt t,\\\\\n T_*:=\\max_i\\|\\mathop{\\mathrm{diag}}(h_{ij})_j h\\|\\le Ct^{\\delta/4},\\qquad\n \\|r\\|_\\infty\\le C,\\qquad \\|u\\|_\\infty\\le t^\\beta.\n\\end{gathered}$$ Here $u=P(g_{\\mathrm{diag}}-r)$.           "exact_quote": "Suppose a committed stage state satisfies the complete stage-boundary bounds of Section <a href=\"#sec:state\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:state\">2</a>, including the broad bounds and comparators <a href=\"#eq:comparators\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:comparators\">[eq:comparators]</a>, the self-consistency relation $r_i=g_{ii}$, the fourth-power bound $H_*=t^{1+\\delta}$, the boundary cap $\\|K_{\\rm old}\\|\\le1/3$, and <a href=\"#eq:local-metric-input\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:local-metric-input\">[eq:local-metric-input]</a>. Assume also that at least $N/2$ physical sites are active, where $N$ is the torus volume, and assume the conditional slot and scalar interface above. Let $\\theta\\in[.25,.625]$ be the reserve fraction, so the new damping scale is $t'=\\theta t$. This includes $\\theta=t_{n+1}/t_n$ at ordinary stages and $\\theta=1/2$ in the final residual sweep. Set $w=1-\\theta$ and use port weights $k_{\\rm bit}=w^{1/4}$, $k_{\\rm reserve}=\\theta^{1/4}$ in Lemma <a href=\"#lem:duplication\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:duplication\">11</a>. Queried variables in port normalization are real variables satisfying the conditional moment and size assumptions above. If every failed trial is followed by a retry supplied with a new independent permutation and fresh inputs satisfying this interface, the trial process terminates almost surely. The indexed auxiliary signs supply these retries for digit sweeps; the actual final sweep instead aborts at its first failure.           "exact_quote": "Suppose the active inverse $g$, with frozen $r,p$, satisfies $$|g_{ii}|+|r_i|\\le C,\\qquad\n c\\le p_i\\le C,\\qquad\n |g_{ii}-r_i|\\le Ct^{\\beta_w},\\qquad\n \\sum_j|h_{ij}|^4\\le H_*$$ at the prestate of a heat, where $h=\\sqrt t\\,g$.           "exact_quote": "Consider an adapted procedure using the ridge rule above, with heats only at positive ridge and at prestates satisfying Lemma <a href=\"#lem:leverage-drift\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:leverage-drift\">30</a>.           "exact_quote": "At post-sweep stage $j\\le\\lfloor m/2\\rfloor$, put $$R_j=4^{8j},\\qquad \\ell_j=4^{4j},\\qquad\n r_*=t_j^{-\\nu},\\qquad n_h=\\lfloor t_j^{-1-e_h}\\rfloor,\n \\qquad e_h=.46\\delta.$$ Take the snapshot components of pending sites joined at distance at most $R_j$, and consider only components $B$ of size at most $r_*$. For $D_s\\asymp t^{-8-\\nu}$, each $O_a$ lies in the ball of radius $D_s$ about its anchor $z_a$ and has size at most $Cn_h$, where $n_h=\\lfloor t^{-1-.46\\delta}\\rfloor$. The anchors are distinct. Extend each $L_a$ by zero to $A_0$. Then $$\\left|\\sum_{a=1}^k L_a\\right|\n \\le t^{.10\\delta}D_0\n \\label{eq:assembly-energy-output}$$ in quadratic forms. In particular, writing $X_k=D_k^+$, every neutral charge $y$ supported in $A_k$ satisfies $$(1+t^{.10\\delta})^{-1}X_0(y)\n \\le X_k(y)\\le\n (1-t^{.10\\delta})^{-1}X_0(y),\n \\label{eq:assembly-inverse-output}$$ where $y$ is extended by zero in $X_0(y)$. <a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-fixed-coupling-spectral-purity**: For each fixed admissible dimension and sufficiently small fixed positive coupling, the stated energy interval has purely absolutely continuous spectrum and nonzero spectral weight. The interval is independent of the coupling.
- **invariant-retained-query-freshness**: Unqueried true digits and unused auxiliary signs retain their conditional product laws. Numerical rollback does not erase observed answers or restore freshness to queried coordinates.
- **invariant-core-completion-range-control**: Deterministic core completion is controlled by the full scattering cross-block range projection. Small nonzero singular amplitudes do not justify discarding their range directions.
- **invariant-own-site-averaging-independence**: Own-site spectral averaging applies conditionally when the complementary operator and hopping vector are independent of the averaged site value. The purity argument uses an exceptional energy set determined by the complementary configuration.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-diffusion-or-mobility-edge**: Read spectral purity as a quantitative diffusion law or a determination of the full mobility edge. -> The spectral conclusion supplies neither a diffusion coefficient nor the location of the full transition between spectral regimes.
- **anti-use-effective-disorder-threshold**: Treat the finite-box threshold specification as a terminating numerical procedure that returns an admissible disorder bound. -> The definition requires an infinite family of probability conditions, and the existence proof supplies no effective numerical upper bound on its threshold integer.
- **anti-use-rollback-restores-randomness**: Reuse a true digit or residual as fresh randomness after rolling back a failed numerical trial. -> The answer remains in the retained history, so its conditional law is no longer the untouched input law required by the update estimates.
- **anti-use-truncated-scattering-range**: Replace the full scattering range by singular directions whose amplitudes exceed a numerical cutoff. -> A direction with small nonzero singular amplitude can still concentrate at a surviving site and invalidate the completion target.
- **anti-use-positive-boundary-values-alone**: Conclude spectral purity solely from positive imaginary boundary values at almost every energy. -> Singular spectral mass can remain supported on an exceptional energy set of Lebesgue measure zero.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The target is almost-sure spectral purity for an infinite lattice operator, obtained through a boundary limit and conditional spectral averaging. The finite-matrix constructions do not supply a finite decision procedure for that conclusion or an effective disorder threshold. At pm-h-81 the source states: The existence proof supplies no effective numerical upper bound for $n_*(d)$. Definition stmt-def-threshold universally quantifies over finite-box scales, normalized disorder parameters, and energies. A finite collection of matrix examples cannot decide these hypotheses or certify exclusion of singular mass in the infinite-volume limit.

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-fixed-dimensional-uniform-lattice-model** (hypothesis): The spectral conclusion is restricted to the stated nearest-neighbor lattice operator with independent uniform site potentials in a fixed admissible dimension. Blocked use: ['Transfer the conclusion to arbitrary graphs, correlated disorder, or other potential distributions without another proof.', 'Apply the delocalization conclusion outside the stated dimension regime.']
- **limit-fixed-weak-positive-coupling** (hypothesis): The almost-sure conclusion holds separately for each fixed positive coupling below the dimension-dependent threshold. Blocked use: ['Assert the conclusion at strong disorder.', 'Claim a common probability-one event for every coupling from the stated fixed-coupling assertion.']
- **limit-selected-energy-window** (counterexample_scope): The absolutely continuous conclusion concerns the specified open interval; at the same coupling a separate lower-edge interval has localized pure-point spectrum. Blocked use: ['Extend spectral purity of the stated type to the entire spectrum.', 'Treat the localized edge interval as part of the absolutely continuous interval.']
- **limit-no-dimension-uniformity** (formal_scope): Constants and smallness thresholds may depend on the fixed dimension. Blocked use: ['Use the estimates as dimension-independent bounds.', 'Take an increasing-dimension limit with unchanged constants.']
- **limit-no-diffusion-or-full-mobility-edge** (formal_scope): Spectral purity on the chosen interval supplies neither a quantitative diffusion law nor the full mobility-edge location. Blocked use: ['Infer a diffusion coefficient, conductivity estimate, or transport rate.', 'Claim the full transition between localized and absolutely continuous spectral regimes has been located.']
- **limit-ineffective-threshold-specification** (nonconstructive): The intrinsic threshold is defined through an infinite family of finite-matrix probability conditions, and its existence proof supplies no effective numerical bound. Blocked use: ['Treat the threshold definition as a terminating numerical search.', 'Certify an admissible coupling by checking only a finite collection of boxes or energies.']
- **limit-initialization-window-and-smallness** (hypothesis): The initial scalar fixed point and comparison slack require the prescribed energy window, scale relation, and sufficiently weak coupling. Uniqueness is asserted inside the displayed rectangle. Blocked use: ['Claim global uniqueness of the scalar equation.', 'Initialize an arbitrary energy or damping value without checking the initialization hypotheses.']
- **limit-retained-history-survives-rollback** (hypothesis): Numerical rollback leaves observed answers in the increasing retained history. It cannot restore the untouched conditional law of a queried coordinate. Blocked use: ['Reuse an exposed true digit as a fresh input after failure.', 'Condition update estimates on the numerical state while omitting retained failed-query answers.']
- **limit-pending-does-not-imply-queried** (edge_case): Pending is a conservative mark withdrawing freshness guarantees, including at sites whose own next digit was never queried. Blocked use: ['Equate the pending set with exactly the queried sites.', 'Leave unreached active sites coupled after a failed first tile trial.']
- **limit-virtual-ports-are-not-an-inverse** (formal_scope): The virtual port matrix repeats and rescales entries of a physical inverse; it is not itself an inverse on the duplicated space. Blocked use: ['Invert the virtual duplicated matrix as though it were a nonsingular physical resolvent.', 'Interpret deletion of a bit port as terminal elimination of its physical site.']
- **limit-ordinary-update-conditional-interface** (hypothesis): Ordinary update estimates require the stated conditional centeredness, variance, and bounded size at the full retained pre-query history, together with the valid prestate bounds. Blocked use: ['Use unconditional moments as a substitute for the conditional update law.', 'Apply the increment estimates after conditioning on future trial acceptance.', 'Use a biased or previously inspected true input as the prescribed fresh scalar.']
- **limit-stopping-includes-breaking-update** (formal_scope): Stopped trial bounds include the update that first violates a budget. Valid prestate hypotheses must justify that prospective update without assuming its poststate satisfies the fine caps. Blocked use: ['Discard the breaking increment from the probability estimate.', 'Justify existence of a failing poststate by assuming the very cap being tested.']
- **limit-scalar-variance-envelope** (hypothesis): The maximal matrix concentration estimate uses deterministic jump and total-variance bounds with predictable scalar envelopes dominating conditional matrix squares. Blocked use: ['Replace the scalar identity envelopes by arbitrary matrix-valued variance data without another concentration argument.', 'Apply the bound to nonadapted increments or envelopes chosen after observing the update.']
- **limit-neutral-charge-schur-comparison** (formal_scope): Inverse-form comparisons across elimination are restricted to survivor-supported neutral charges, extended by zero to the earlier space. Blocked use: ['Read the inverse-form identity as equality of full pseudoinverse matrices.', 'Evaluate the claimed quotient inverse on nonneutral charges.']
- **limit-full-scattering-range** (hypothesis): Core completion requires control of the full cross-block range projection. Small nonzero singular values do not justify discarding their directions. Blocked use: ['Replace the full range by a numerically truncated singular subspace without an additional error proof.', 'Use small raw cross-block row norms as a substitute for the projection-diagonal target.']
- **limit-clearing-eligible-exterior-and-core** (hypothesis): Preparation requires eligible localized exterior pivots with untouched true residuals, trial-start slack, and the prescribed core-size and geometry bounds. Deterministic core completion additionally needs a nonempty exterior and the relevant true terminal inverses. Blocked use: ['Use the residual law at an arbitrary exterior site.', 'Complete a core without checking its projection target and terminal invertibility.', 'Assume the true core values themselves must be fresh centered inputs.']
- **limit-committed-versus-provisional-bounds** (formal_scope): The transported comparison bounds and correction-operator cap are conclusions for committed numerical states. They are not assumed at intermediate provisional heat prefixes. Blocked use: ['Apply committed-state Laplacian comparisons inside an arbitrary clearing heat prefix.', 'Accumulate analytic error from rolled-back failed trials as though they were committed operations.']
- **limit-reset-is-local-self-consistency** (hypothesis): The diagonal reset requires a nonempty active set, positive bounded imaginary coefficients, the constant Laplacian kernel, small lag, and the stated correction and inverse-row bounds. Blocked use: ['Treat the reset as a global solver for arbitrary diagonal self-consistency equations.', 'Reset after the final true-suffix sweep as part of the stated construction.']
- **limit-birth-product-bound-is-not-independence** (formal_scope): Joint failure bounds are obtained by successive conditioning for distinct deterministic labels. Spatial separation ensures distinct witness leaves rather than independence of failures. Blocked use: ['Model births as independent events.', 'Apply the product bound directly to an adaptively selected witness without summing over deterministic possibilities.']
- **limit-final-certificate-uses-only-true-potentials** (hypothesis): The final certificate requires every real site value to be an original true potential. Auxiliary digits used during earlier retries do not remain in its endpoint Hamiltonian. Blocked use: ['Pass an auxiliary-potential endpoint to the true-operator spectral readout.', 'Retry a failed final sweep with auxiliary suffixes under the stated construction.']
- **limit-averaging-under-unconditional-true-law** (hypothesis): Adaptive certificate feasibility is compatible with the spectral comparison, but the rank estimate is averaged under the unconditional true product law. Blocked use: ['Assume site potentials remain independent after conditioning on certificate success.', 'Require independence between the selected damping set and the true potentials as an unstated substitute.']
- **limit-boundary-positivity-does-not-alone-prove-purity** (formal_scope): Positive imaginary boundary values almost everywhere do not alone exclude singular spectral mass. The complementary exceptional energy set must be independent of the remaining site variable before own-site averaging removes its mass. Blocked use: ['Conclude spectral purity from almost-everywhere boundary positivity alone.', 'Average over an exceptional set selected using the same site variable being averaged.']
- **limit-finite-experiments-cannot-certify-main-result** (nonconstructive): Finite matrix tests can check particular algebraic identities or candidate certificates, but cannot decide the infinite-volume spectral conclusion or its universally quantified threshold specification. Blocked use: ['Report a finite numerical experiment as a certificate of the main almost-sure theorem.', 'Treat successful small matrix examples as proof that exceptional singular mass is absent.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


For each fixed dimension <i>d</i> ≥ 3 and each fixed sufficiently small positive disorder strength, we prove that the Anderson operator on ℤ<sup><i>d</i></sup> with independent uniform site potentials almost surely has purely absolutely continuous spectrum with nonzero weight on an open energy interval. The interval may depend on <i>d</i> but is independent of the disorder strength. This settles the purely absolutely continuous energy-range question in Simon's Problem 1 for this model.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

The Anderson model asks how independent disorder changes the spectral and transport properties of a lattice Hamiltonian. We prove a weak-disorder delocalization result for independent uniform site potentials in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$: on a fixed open interval, the spectrum is purely absolutely continuous and has nonzero weight. Both eigenvalue mass and singular continuous mass are excluded.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The model and the result

<a id="eq:model"></a>
Fix an integer $d\ge3$. On the product probability space $$\Omega=[-1,1]^{\mathbb Z^d},\qquad
 \mathbb P=\left(\tfrac12\mathbf1_{[-1,1]}(v)\,dv\right)^{\otimes\mathbb Z^d},$$ let $V_x(\omega)=\omega_x$. For $\lambda>0$, define the bounded self-adjoint operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^d)$ by $$\label{eq:model}
 (H_{\lambda,\omega}\psi)(x)
 =-\sum_{j=1}^d\bigl(\psi(x+\mathbf e_j)+\psi(x-\mathbf e_j)\bigr)
   +\lambda V_x(\omega)\psi(x).$$ Here $\mathbf e_1,\ldots,\mathbf e_d$ are the coordinate vectors. Multiplication by $(-1)^{x_1+\cdots+x_d}$ is a unitary operator that reverses the hopping sign and leaves the diagonal potential unchanged. Thus the positive-hopping convention gives the identical conclusion. For a Borel set $B$, write $\chi_B(H)$ for the spectral projection, and let $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ be the subspace of vectors whose spectral measures are absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

<a id="eq:energy-windows"></a>
**Theorem 1**. *There is a fixed sufficiently small number $e_2\in(0,1/100)$ such that, for every fixed integer $d\ge3$, there is a number $\lambda_d>0$ with the following property. Set $$\label{eq:energy-windows}
 I_d=
 \begin{cases}
   (-6+e_2/2,-6+e_2),&d=3,\\
   -2d+(1/200,1/100),&d\ge4.
 \end{cases}$$ Then for every fixed $0<\lambda<\lambda_d$, almost surely $$I_d\subset\sigma(H_{\lambda,\omega}),\qquad
 \chi_{I_d}(H_{\lambda,\omega})\ell^2(\mathbb Z^d)
       \subset\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{\lambda,\omega}).$$ In particular, the spectral restriction to $I_d$ is purely absolutely continuous and $\chi_{I_d}(H_{\lambda,\omega})\ne0$. For $d\ge4$, one may take $\lambda_d=\sqrt3\,2^{-n_*(d)}$, where the finite-matrix specification of $n_*(d)$ is given in Definition <a href="#def:threshold" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:threshold">39</a>. For $d=3$, the proof supplies an existential positive threshold.*

</div>

The interval is independent of $\lambda$. The probability-one event may depend on the fixed coupling, and all estimates may depend on the fixed dimension. No uniformity as $d\to\infty$ is asserted. The integer $n_*(d)$ for $d\ge4$ is specified by an infinite family of probability conditions on finite matrices. The proof establishes its existence but supplies no effective numerical bound.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### Historical context and scope

Anderson’s random-site-energy model explains how spatial disorder can suppress quantum transport (Anderson 1958) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[Anderson1958](#ref-Anderson1958)]. The competing weak-disorder question is whether extended states survive on a Euclidean lattice of dimension at least three. Simon’s Problem 1 asks for a purely absolutely continuous energy range for the nearest-neighbor model with iid uniform potentials in dimensions at least three, at suitable disorder widths (Simon 2000) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Simon2000](#ref-Simon2000)]. Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a> supplies the purely absolutely continuous energy range requested in that problem for every sufficiently small fixed disorder width in each fixed dimension $d\ge3$. It does not locate the full mobility edge discussed after Problem 1 or resolve the diffusion question stated separately as Problem 3.

Rigorous localization was developed through several complementary methods. Fröhlich and Spencer introduced a multiscale Green-function analysis in strong-disorder and suitable extreme-energy regimes (Fröhlich and Spencer 1983) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[FrohlichSpencer1983](#ref-FrohlichSpencer1983)]; Fröhlich, Martinelli, Scoppola and Spencer subsequently established pure-point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions in such regimes (Fröhlich et al. 1985) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[FMSS1985](#ref-FMSS1985)]. The fractional-moment method of Aizenman and Molchanov gives another route to spectral localization at large disorder and extreme energies (Aizenman and Molchanov 1993) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[AizenmanMolchanov1993](#ref-AizenmanMolchanov1993)]. Corollary <a href="#cor:coexistence" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cor:coexistence">2</a> combines a fixed-disorder edge-localization theorem with Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a> at the same coupling. A localized edge interval alone does not determine the spectral type throughout the rest of the band.

On the Bethe lattice, Klein proved purely absolutely continuous spectrum on compact intervals inside the free band at sufficiently weak disorder (Klein 1994, 1998) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[Klein1994](#ref-Klein1994), [Klein1998](#ref-Klein1998)]. Aizenman, Sims and Warzel established stability of the absolutely continuous component by a fluctuation-based method (Aizenman, Sims, and Warzel 2006) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[AizenmanSimsWarzel2006](#ref-AizenmanSimsWarzel2006)]; that result does not itself assert spectral purity. Aizenman and Warzel used resonant delocalization to obtain an absolutely continuous component beyond the free band for regular full-support laws at weak disorder, and proved pure absolute continuity near the spectral edges in a weak bounded-disorder regime that includes the uniform law (Aizenman and Warzel 2013) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[AizenmanWarzel2013](#ref-AizenmanWarzel2013)]. For sufficiently high-degree trees, at a specified hopping scale and for a regular class of full-support single-site densities, Aggarwal and Lopatto obtained mobility edges separating absolutely continuous and pure-point intervals (Aggarwal and Lopatto 2025) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[AggarwalLopatto2025](#ref-AggarwalLopatto2025)]. The branching geometry distinguishes these results from the model on $\mathbb Z^d$; the last result also has different law and scale assumptions.

Jakšić, Last and Warzel gave a further tree argument and a conditional lattice criterion through the Schur complement of a two-site Poisson-transformed spectral measure (Jakšić, Last, and Warzel 2026) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[JaksicLastWarzel2026](#ref-JaksicLastWarzel2026)]. Their criterion assumes a positive lower limit of the expected energy-integrated quantity and concludes a nontrivial absolutely continuous component. It does not establish that lower bound for the present weak-disorder lattice model.

Erdős, Salmhofer and Yau proved a weak-coupling diffusion limit for the lattice model: at disorder-dependent long times and spatial scales, the expected Wigner distribution converges to a heat-equation solution as the coupling tends to zero (Erdős, Salmhofer, and Yau 2007) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[ErdosSalmhoferYau2007](#ref-ErdosSalmhoferYau2007)]. For Gaussian disorder, Black, Drogin and Hernández obtained estimates at long finite times and positive resolvent heights in a weak-coupling regime (Black, Drogin, and Hernández 2025) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[BlackDroginHernandez2025](#ref-BlackDroginHernandez2025)]. Here the boundary limit is taken at each fixed sufficiently small positive coupling, and the conclusion also excludes singular spectral mass.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### The proof mechanism

The proof first establishes a finite-volume resolvent certificate. On a large periodic lattice, we construct a set containing at least half the sites and add small complex damping only on that set. The diagonal imaginary parts there remain bounded below as the damping tends to zero. At each site, the final real potential is its original independent uniform variable. Proposition <a href="#prop:certificate" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:certificate">3</a> states the certificate precisely.

We begin with the free operator and write each uniform potential as a series of independent binary signs. Revealing a sign replaces part of the artificial damping by true randomness. Active sites retain damping; terminal sites have their complete true potentials and have been eliminated by a Schur complement. During a stage, a diagonal self-consistency parameter remains frozen until the stage-end reset. We carry three controls for the rescaled inverse on active physical sites. Its complex entrywise square controls the linearized equation for the eventual diagonal reset. A bound on row fourth moments prevents the mass of a resolvent row from concentrating at a few sites, limiting the influence of individual updates. The Ward identity turns squared absolute resolvent entries into a Laplacian whose inverse form supplies a spatial energy norm for accumulating local changes. Fourier estimates for the free resolvent initialize these bounds with slack on the chosen energy interval.

During the one-digit stages, ordinary updates are tested on finite tiles, since a union bound over all sites at all scales would be too expensive. A coupled active site carries a true prefix with an untouched suffix, and a first tile trial uses its next true sign when that site is reached. If an ordinary tile trial fails, its numerical changes are rolled back and every answer remains in the retained information. All active sites in that tile are marked *pending*, including sites not reached by the trial. The mark is conservative: at a pending site the construction ceases to rely on the true-prefix and untouched-suffix guarantees. Ordinary updates at pending sites use independent auxiliary digits; a retry uses new ones throughout the tile.

At later scales we clear small components of pending sites. A unitary scattering matrix records the interaction between a fixed core and its exterior. The range of its cross block contains the survivor directions through which completing the core can act. Unitarity bounds the size of that change, so small diagonal entries of the projection onto the cross-block range make its effect small in every surviving row. This gives a deterministic target for preparing the core, with no freshness assumption on the core values.

Regularized projection weights guide exposures of true residuals at exterior sites. A spatial estimate controls the entire cross-block range even when its nonzero singular values are arbitrarily small; together with component separation and the retained marking rules, it keeps selected exterior pivots close to their core and ensures that their true residuals are still untouched. A negative drift bounds the number of exposures, while stopped martingale estimates control their accumulated effect, including a first violating update. After successful preparation, any still-unknown true core values are revealed and recorded, and the deterministic completion is applied. The core and exposed exterior sites then become committed terminals. A failed clearing rolls back its provisional matrix changes, keeps every answer, and marks its core and every inspected exterior site pending.

Two inductions connect these operations to the certificate. A deterministic induction combines committed local changes, controls the geometry of terminal sites, keeps at least half the sites active, and closes the self-consistent reset. A probabilistic induction tracks the retained information and bounds failures at deterministically ordered labels by successive conditioning. A surviving pending site yields either a recent failure label or many separated older witnesses whose leaf labels are distinct. With high probability the cutoff finds no pending sites and the later sweeps succeed. The last sweep then inserts the entire remaining true suffix at every active site. Those sites keep the final small damping, although their real potentials are now complete true values.

The spectral argument converts the certificate to information about the ordinary resolvent of the true operator. A cut by its spectral projection onto a narrow energy window controls the comparison through that projection’s rank for every qualifying certificate. Own-site averaging under the original product law of the true potentials bounds the expected rank, giving a positive expectation for a bounded function of the true scalar diagonal imaginary part. That estimate passes to infinite volume. At almost every fixed energy, ergodicity and rank-one changes of a site potential then propagate boundary positivity to every site almost surely. Conditioning on the operator with one site removed produces an exceptional energy set independent of the remaining site variable. Absolute continuity holds on its complement, and spectral averaging removes mass on the exceptional set itself. This final step gives purity.

The form of the construction is common to all fixed $d\ge3$. Dimension enters through three estimates. A deliberately weaker Fourier bound retains the three-dimensional interpolation gains in every dimension, with a convex-slice argument handling two-resolvent shell tangencies. The allowed size exponent for pending components is chosen inversely proportional to $d$, keeping spatial packing losses below the analytic gains. The history recursion uses a dimension-dependent separation of scales to pay for the possible positions of spatial witnesses.

Related resolvent controls appear in Black, Drogin and Hernández’s work on the Gaussian Anderson model: a self-consistent diagonal shift, concentration governed by fourth-power row sums, and an elliptic equation for averaged squared resolvent entries (Black, Drogin, and Hernández 2025, secs. 1.1–1.2) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[BlackDroginHernandez2025](#ref-BlackDroginHernandez2025)]. Their spatial equation develops the $T$-equation approach of Erdős, Knowles, Yau and Yin for random band matrices (Erdős et al. 2013) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[ErdosKnowlesYauYin2013](#ref-ErdosKnowlesYauYin2013)]. Here the Ward identity gives an exact Laplacian for each current matrix state, and we transport its inverse form and the other controls through the adaptive revelations.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
#### Coexistence with edge localization

The interval $I_d$ lies above the lower free band edge $-2d$. At the lower edge of the almost-sure spectrum, fixed-disorder localization gives a separate interval. Combining that result with Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a> yields the following consequence at the same fixed coupling.

<a id="stmt-cor-coexistence"></a>
<div id="cor:coexistence" class="corollary">

**Corollary 2** (Spectral coexistence). *For every fixed $d\ge3$ and every fixed $0<\lambda<\lambda_d$, there is a deterministic number $\delta_{d,\lambda}\in(0,\lambda/2]$ such that the open interval $$J_{d,\lambda}
 =(-2d-\lambda,-2d-\lambda+\delta_{d,\lambda})$$ is disjoint from $I_d$ and, almost surely, both $\chi_{I_d}(H_{\lambda,\omega})$ and $\chi_{J_{d,\lambda}}(H_{\lambda,\omega})$ are nonzero. The restriction to $I_d$ is purely absolutely continuous, whereas the restriction to $J_{d,\lambda}$ is pure point with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions. The probability-one event may depend on $d$ and $\lambda$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cor-coexistence"><summary>Proof of stmt-cor-coexistence</summary>

*Proof.* The variables $\lambda V_x$ have the iid law $\mu_\lambda(dv)=(2\lambda)^{-1}\mathbf1_{[-\lambda,\lambda]}(v)\,dv$. Its concentration function is $\sup_a\mu_\lambda([a,a+t])=\min\{1,t/(2\lambda)\}$, so it satisfies the bounded-support Hölder hypothesis of the fixed-disorder edge localization theorem of Elgart and Klein. Their author-preprint Theorem 2.2 and Corollary 1.8(i)–(ii) (Elgart and Klein 2019) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[ElgartKlein2019](#ref-ElgartKlein2019)] give a deterministic $A>0$ and almost-sure pure-point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions on $[-2d-\lambda,-2d-\lambda+A)$. Take $\delta_{d,\lambda}=\min\{A/2,\lambda/2\}$. The almost-sure spectrum is $[-2d-\lambda,2d+\lambda]$ (Elgart and Klein 2019, author-preprint equation (1.17)) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[ElgartKlein2019](#ref-ElgartKlein2019)], hence its projection on the nonempty open interval $J_{d,\lambda}$ cannot vanish. This interval lies below $-2d$, while $I_d$ lies above $-2d$. Intersect the localization and spectrum events with the probability-one event of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>, at the same fixed coupling. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
###### Organization.

Section <a href="#sec:state" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:state">2</a> sets up the certificate and matrix states. Section <a href="#sec:initialization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:initialization">3</a> initializes the invariant bounds. Sections <a href="#sec:sweep" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:sweep">4</a> and <a href="#sec:local-sweeps" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:local-sweeps">5</a> establish ordinary updates and their stopped local trials. Sections <a href="#sec:clearing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:clearing">6</a> and <a href="#sec:assembly" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:assembly">7</a> prepare pending cores, combine the committed changes, and close the deterministic induction. Section <a href="#sec:history" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:history">8</a> controls the retained failures and completes the finite-volume certificate and the threshold specification. Section <a href="#sec:spectral" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:spectral">9</a> converts the certificate to Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>.

<a id="sec:state"></a>
### A finite-volume certificate and the matrix state

The construction will produce a certificate for a damped resolvent of the finite Anderson matrix with the true potentials. We state that target first, then describe the numerical state and the information retained while the potential is revealed. Each finite-volume construction fixes the energy and coupling; its event may depend on both, while its probability estimate is uniform in the energy interval. Throughout the proof $d\ge3$ is a fixed integer. Constants denoted by $c,C$, including constants implicit in $O(\cdot)$ and $\asymp$, may depend on $d$ and the fixed interval $I_d$. No assertion is uniform as $d\to\infty$.

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
#### The certificate

<a id="eq:scales"></a>
Fix the interval $I_d$ from <a href="#eq:energy-windows" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:energy-windows">[eq:energy-windows]</a>, a coupling $0<\lambda<1$, and integers $$\label{eq:scales}
 \begin{aligned}
 n_0&=\lfloor\log_4(3/\lambda^2)\rfloor,\qquad m\ge4n_0,\\
 s_n&=\frac{\lambda^2}{3}4^{n_0-n}\quad(n_0\le n\le m),\\
 \eta&=s_m,\qquad t_n=s_n+\eta.
 \end{aligned}$$ Equivalently, if $u=(\lambda^2/3)4^{n_0}\in(1/4,1]$, then $s_n=u4^{-n}$ and $\eta=u4^{-m}$. Thus $\frac14 4^{-n}<s_n\le4^{-n}$ and $t_n\asymp4^{-n}$, with absolute comparison constants. Let $$L=4^{20m},\qquad \mathbb T_L=(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d,\qquad N=L^d,$$ and let $H_m$ be the periodic version of <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a>, in the negative-hopping convention: $$(H_m f)(i)=-\sum_{|e|_1=1}f(i+e)+\lambda V_i f(i),
 \qquad V_i\ \text{independent and uniform on }[-1,1].$$ There is an independent potential at every point of this $d$-dimensional torus. For $A\subset\mathbb T_L$, write $P_A$ for coordinate restriction or projection, as indicated by its domain, and let $\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}_A r$ be the full matrix with diagonal $r_i$ on $A$ and zero elsewhere.

<a id="stmt-prop-certificate"></a>
<div id="prop:certificate" class="proposition">

**Proposition 3** (Finite-volume certificate). *For each fixed $d\ge3$ there exist $\lambda_0(d)>0$ and constants $c,C>0$ with the following property. For every fixed $0<\lambda<\lambda_0(d)$, every $E\in I_d$, and every $m\ge4n_0$, one can use auxiliary independent randomness to construct an event $\mathcal S_m$, depending on the fixed $E,\lambda$, such that $\mathbb P(\mathcal S_m)\to1$ as $m\to\infty$. On $\mathcal S_m$ there are a set $A\subset\mathbb T_L$, $|A|\ge N/2$, and complex numbers $r_i$, $i\in A$, satisfying $$|r_i|\le C,\qquad c\le\Im r_i\le C,$$ such that $$\widehat G=(H_m-E-\eta\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}_A r)^{-1}
 \quad\text{exists},\qquad
 \Im\widehat G_{ii}\ge c\quad(i\in A).$$ For fixed $d$ the constants are independent of $E,\lambda,m$, and the convergence in probability is uniform in $E\in I_d$ for each fixed $\lambda$. The failure estimates are also uniformly small for all $m\ge4n_0$ and $u\in(1/4,1]$ once $n_0$ is sufficiently large. The potential in $H_m$ consists entirely of the original true variables.*

</div>

The proof occupies Sections <a href="#sec:initialization" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:initialization">3</a>–<a href="#sec:history" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:history">8</a>. Section <a href="#sec:spectral" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:spectral">9</a> proves that this certificate implies Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>. The true potential vector retains its original product law as an unconditional marginal of the enlarged probability space. The success event may depend on that vector. The spectral proof uses a feasibility event in the true variables and unconditional averaging.

<a id="pm-h-10"></a>
#### True digits, site states, and retained information

A uniform random variable $\lambda V_i$ has the representation <a id="eq:history-binary"></a>$$\lambda V_i=\sum_{k\ge1}\lambda2^{-k}\varepsilon_{i,k},
 \qquad \mathbb P(\varepsilon_{i,k}=1)
       =\mathbb P(\varepsilon_{i,k}=-1)=\tfrac12,
 \label{eq:history-binary}$$ with independent signs over all sites and indices. Resolve the possible binary ambiguity on its null set by a fixed convention. After the first $h$ signs at a site have been exposed, and before any further information about that site has been queried, its remaining sum is uniform on $[-\lambda2^{-h},\lambda2^{-h}]$, with mean zero and variance $\lambda^2 4^{-h}/3$. In particular, after $n-n_0$ digits its variance is $s_n$, and its next digit has amplitude $\sqrt{3s_n/4}$.

At each committed state the physical sites are partitioned into an active set $A$ and a terminal set $T$. Active sites retain artificial damping. A committed terminal site has its exact true potential, has been Schur-eliminated, and never changes again. During the one-digit stages an active site’s real potential value is partial. At the final endpoint, the active sites carry complete true potentials while retaining damping.

A subset of the active sites is marked *pending*; a nonpending active site is *coupled*. Before the final residual sweep, the construction maintains the following implication: at a coupled site the installed partial value is exactly the true revealed prefix, and no digit of its remaining suffix has been queried. At a stage boundary this prefix has $n-n_0$ digits; during a one-digit sweep it has one more digit at sites already processed. The final sweep installs the entire remaining true suffix. A pending site’s partial value may contain auxiliary digits, and the construction makes no freshness claim for its true suffix. The mark is conservative: the marking rule can cover an active site whose own next digit was not queried. A pending site can leave this class only by becoming terminal.

The numerical matrices and the information already revealed are separate records. Inside a trial, newly terminal physical sites and other matrix changes are provisional until the trial commits. A failure restores the pretrial potential values and partition into active and terminal sites, together with the corresponding matrices, and then applies the trial’s marking rule for pending sites. All answers already obtained remain in the retained history. Previously committed terminal sites remain permanent.

<figure id="fig:site-states">

<figcaption>The arrows show possible changes between committed site states. A pending mark is conservative: the marked site’s own true suffix may remain unqueried. The final suffix sweep is reached only when no site is pending; after it succeeds, the active sites have complete true potentials and retain artificial damping.</figcaption>
</figure>

  >=Stealth,thick]

\node[state] (pending) at (0,-1.35) {Pending active\\\small may use auxiliary digits};
\node[state,fill=black!9] (terminal) at (7.8,0) {Committed terminal\\\small complete true potential\\\small permanent};
\draw[->] (coupled) -- node[lab,right]{failed trial} (pending);
\draw[->] (pending.east) -- node[lab,below,sloped]{successful clearing} (terminal.south west);
\draw[->] (coupled.east) -- node[lab,above,sloped]{included in a\\successful clearing} (terminal.north west);
\draw[densely dashed,black!40] (-2.35,-2.30) rectangle (2.35,2.30);
\node[font=\small,anchor=south] at (0,2.32) {Active sites retain artificial damping};

Initially every site is active and coupled, and every partial value is zero. The retained-information lemma below supplies the conditional law of an unqueried input. Sections <a href="#sec:local-sweeps" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:local-sweeps">5</a> and <a href="#sec:assembly" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:assembly">7</a> verify that the inputs selected by ordinary trials and clearings are eligible for that law. In the matrix estimates, “fresh” means a centered variable with the stated law conditional on the history available before the chosen update. It is an explicit input until the corresponding eligibility check has been made.

<a id="pm-h-11"></a>
###### Retained information.

The construction uses a separate countable array of independent auxiliary fair signs. It also uses independent uniform orders of fixed finite sets: a uniform order of a set $S$ of size $M$ is a uniformly chosen bijection from $\{1,\ldots,M\}$ to $S$. All these sources are independent of the true signs and of one another. Only an auxiliary sign that is used, or the next entry of an order being used, is exposed. Section <a href="#sec:local-sweeps" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:local-sweeps">5</a> specifies the source indices for each ordinary trial.

Number the successive queries and completed measurable decisions by $q=1,2,\ldots$, and let $\mathcal F_q^{\mathrm{ret}}$ be the information retained after operation $q$. Initially $\mathcal F_0^{\mathrm{ret}}$ contains only the fixed parameters and deterministic initial data. A completed measurable numerical choice counts as one operation even when it is defined by a limit, as with the later ridge choice or diagonal reset. Before a query, its type and source index are chosen measurably from the current history. A query may expose one true digit, one unused auxiliary sign, the remaining true suffix at a selected site, or the next entry of a selected finite order that has an unexposed entry. A whole true suffix is one operation; under the fixed binary convention, its value determines all the digits it contains. The history records the queried indices and answers and every exposed order entry. Numerical updates, choices, and failure decisions must be measurable from the information recorded by that time, so adjoining them gives no further information.

The current potential values, active and terminal sets, pending marks, and matrices are measurable functions of this retained history. Rollback and marking are measurable operations, and the sigma-fields $\mathcal F_q^{\mathrm{ret}}$ continue to increase: answers observed in failed trials remain known. Whenever an operation installs an exact true value whose remaining digits have not yet been queried, it first exposes and records that true suffix. This also applies when the change is controlled by a deterministic estimate.

<a id="stmt-lem-conditional-freshness"></a>
<div id="lem:conditional-freshness" class="lemma">

**Lemma 4** (Conditional freshness). *Suppose queries obey the preceding rule. Conditional on the retained history, the unqueried true digits retain their product fair-sign law. The same holds jointly for unused auxiliary signs. In particular, at distinct sites whose remaining true suffixes are unqueried, those suffixes are conditionally independent and have the uniform laws specified above. After a revealed prefix of an independent uniform order, its remaining order is conditionally uniform over the unexposed elements, jointly with the stated product law for unqueried signs.*

*These statements hold after every deterministic finite number of operations and at every almost surely finite stopping time of $(\mathcal F_q^{\mathrm{ret}})$, with conditioning on the stopped sigma-field.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-conditional-freshness"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-conditional-freshness</summary>

*Proof.* Condition on the history before a query. Its source index is then fixed. Coordinates whose values are already recorded contribute no new information. If a query includes both known and unqueried digits, apply the following factorization to its unqueried part. For a sign query, the product law factors into the queried coordinate and the other unqueried coordinates. Adjoining the answer leaves the latter factors unchanged. For a whole true suffix, apply the same argument to its block of digits: test against finite cylinder functions of the other coordinates and then use the monotone class theorem. This is a statement about conditional expectations, so it also covers a continuous residual answer without conditioning on an individual value of probability zero. The same factorization applies to unused auxiliary signs.

For a uniform order with $r$ elements still unexposed, each possible next element has exactly $(r-1)!$ completions. Its remaining order is therefore uniform after that entry is revealed. An answer subsequently queried at the selected index uses no unexposed order entry. Choices and failure decisions made from the enlarged history add no information. Induction proves the assertions after every fixed finite number of operations.

For precision at a random operation time, let $\tau$ be a stopping time of $(\mathcal F_q^{\mathrm{ret}})$ with $\mathbb P(\tau<\infty)=1$, and let $\mathcal F_\tau^{\mathrm{ret}}$ be its stopped sigma-field. For $D\in\mathcal F_\tau^{\mathrm{ret}}$, apply each finite-operation conditional-expectation identity against $D\cap\{\tau=q\}\in\mathcal F_q^{\mathrm{ret}}$ and sum over $q$. These countably many events exhaust $D$ up to a null set and give the same identity conditional on $\mathcal F_\tau^{\mathrm{ret}}$. A whole-suffix query remains one operation in this argument. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-12"></a>
#### Schur reduction and the Ward Laplacian

For the fixed $E$ and $\lambda>0$, almost surely every principal matrix of the true $H_m-E$ is invertible. Indeed, for a nonempty subset its determinant is a polynomial in the independent continuous potentials, with nonzero highest monomial $\prod_{i}\lambda V_i$. Its zero set has Lebesgue measure zero. There are finitely many subsets on the torus. We henceforth work on this event, which also covers subsets chosen adaptively later. This probability-one property is not a preliminary test of unrevealed potentials and supplies no information to the algorithm’s filtration. The empty terminal block requires no inverse.

Let $\mathcal H$ be the real symmetric matrix with the current real potential values on $A$ and exact true values on $T$. Eliminate the terminal block at the real energy $E$, obtaining $$M=(\mathcal H-E)_{AA}
   -(\mathcal H-E)_{AT}(\mathcal H-E)_{TT}^{-1}
                         (\mathcal H-E)_{TA}.$$ The matrix $M$ is real symmetric. Its off-diagonal entries connect nearest neighbors or sites joined through one connected component of terminal sites. Throughout, the subscript in a Schur complement names the *eliminated* indices: if $R$ is the complement of $\mathcal E$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Schur}}_{\mathcal E} B
 =B_{RR}-B_{R\mathcal E}B_{\mathcal E\mathcal E}^{-1}B_{\mathcal ER}.$$ We use this notation only when the displayed inverse exists. Put $r=(r_i)_{i\in A}\in\mathbb C^A$, $p_i=\Im r_i>0$, and, for a scale $t>0$, define $$g=(M-t\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}r)^{-1},\qquad h=\sqrt t\,g,\qquad
 K_{ij}=h_{ij}^2,\quad F_{ij}=|h_{ij}|^2,\quad q_i=\Im g_{ii}.$$ The inverse exists because its matrix has strictly negative imaginary part. In particular $\|g\|\le(t\min p_i)^{-1}$. Both $g$ and $h$ are complex symmetric. For a matrix $B$, $\Im B=(B-B^*)/(2i)$; here it is also the entrywise imaginary part. The resolvent identity gives the Ward identity <a id="eq:ward"></a>$$\label{eq:ward}
 h\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(p)h^*=\Im g,\qquad Fp=q.$$ Consequently $$D=\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(pq)-\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(p)F\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(p)$$ is a real graph Laplacian, with nonnegative edge weights $p_i p_jF_{ij}$. Its quadratic form is $$D(f)=\frac12\sum_{i,j}p_i p_jF_{ij}|f_i-f_j|^2.$$ The nonnegative weights $F_{ij}=|h_{ij}|^2$ describe how the Ward mass is distributed across a row. We use $B(f)=\langle f,Bf\rangle$ for the quadratic form of a Hermitian matrix. At the committed states below, the kernel of $D$ is precisely the constants. Its pseudoinverse $X=D^+$ is then an inverse on neutral charges, namely vectors $y$ with $\sum_i y_i=0$.

We record the precise Schur identity for these inverse forms. If $U$ is eliminated and $R=A\setminus U\ne\varnothing$, then $D_{UU}$ is positive definite: extending a zero-energy vector by zero on $R$ would otherwise give a nonconstant vector in $\ker D$. Moreover, $$(\mathop{\mathrm{Schur}}_U D)(f_R)=\min_{f_U}D(f_R,f_U).$$ It follows that $\mathop{\mathrm{Schur}}_U D$ has only the constant kernel. For a neutral $y$ supported on $R$, extend it by zero to $A$ and use the variational formula $$X(y)=\sup_f\{2\Re\langle y,f\rangle-D(f)\}.$$ Minimizing first over $f_U$ proves <a id="eq:schur-inverse-form"></a>$$\label{eq:schur-inverse-form}
 (\mathop{\mathrm{Schur}}_U D)^+(y)=D^+(y).$$ All later inverse-form comparisons across deletion are understood in this sense, on survivor-supported neutral charges, not as an equality of full pseudoinverse matrices.

At the beginning of a stage the state satisfies $r_i=g_{ii}$. During a sweep or clearing trial, $r$ remains frozen. Thus $q=p$ at the stage boundary, and the difference $g_{ii}-r_i$ measures the subsequent diagonal lag. Because $g$ itself depends on $r$, restoring the equality requires a small self-consistent correction. The stage-end reset in Section <a href="#sec:assembly" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:assembly">7</a> constructs that correction.

The role of $K$ is visible in this self-consistency equation. For the physical active inverse, differentiation with respect to the complex diagonal parameter gives $$\frac{\partial g_{ii}}{\partial r_j}=t g_{ij}^2=K_{ij}.$$ Thus the linearization of $r-(g_{ii}(r))_{i\in A}=0$ is $I-K$, which is invertible whenever $\|K\|<1$.
